summary.title: Function-Aware Fill-in-the-Middle as Mid-Training for Coding Agent Foundation Models

details: Coding agents must integrate externally produced tool returns into ongoing reasoning, but left-to-right code pretraining (and random-span FIM) exposes this conditioning structure only weakly, leaving a gap before agentic post-training.

Claimed structural isomorphism: a function call site (pre-call context, call, externally computed return, downstream usage) mirrors an agent's history, action, observation, continuation loop, making ordinary code an internet-scale source of agent-relevant signal.
Function-aware fill-in-the-middle mid-training: a dedicated self-supervised stage inserted between pretraining and agentic post-training.

Masking targets are whole functions (or 2-3 structurally connected functions) chosen from a program dependency graph via a double criterion combining a hand-designed complexity score (LoC, cyclomatic complexity, nesting depth) and an inferability score (caller/callee/signature/docstring/class context), combined as a harmonic-mean-like product with a one-sided penalty for targets hard even given full context.
A chain-of-thought rationale is placed inside the FIM middle span before the function body, so the model learns think-then-act reasoning consistent with the code it emits.
968 Python GitHub repositories filtered from ~2,000 candidates; decontaminated by removing SWE-Bench source repos/forks and restricting to commits predating the earliest SWE-Bench base commit.
~78K files yield ~400K FIM samples / ~2.6B tokens (320K single-function, 60K pair, 20K triple targets; mean target ~34 LoC).

CoT rationales generated by Gemini-3-Flash from the masked file only (no ground-truth body), then filtered by a Gemini-3-Flash judge on feasibility plus five quality dimensions; ground-truth body used only as filter anchor.
Selection hyperparameters: file lines in [50,1800], function LoC in [10,200], dunder methods excluded, tau_FIM=0.08, tau_H=0.15; group coupling term with 8 topology patterns and per-file caps.
Mid-trained bases: Qwen2.5-Coder-Instruct 7B and 14B, and Qwen3-8B; 1 epoch, lr 1e-5, seq len 32,768, bf16, effective batch 128 on 8xH100.
Agentic post-training applied unmodified afterwards: R2E-Gym and SWE-Smith for Qwen2.5-Coder; SWE-Lego for Qwen3-8B (2 epochs instead of official 4).
Agent harnesses fixed by pipeline: OpenHands fork (R2E-Gym), SWE-agent (SWE-Smith), OpenHands (Qwen3-8B/SWE-Lego).
Primary in-domain: SWE-Bench-Verified (500) and SWE-Bench-Lite (300); means over three evaluation seeds.
Capability-preservation suite (14B + R2E-Gym only): LiveCodeBench, OJBench, FullStackBench-EN, Terminal-Bench 2.0, tau-bench, BFCL.

Baseline = base + post-training (reproduced, with official numbers quoted where available); ours = base + FIM mid-training + identical post-training; mid-training-only checkpoints not evaluated due to degraded instruction following.
CoT source: no CoT vs. self-generated CoT vs. Gemini-3-Flash CoT.
Selection algorithm: random, Gemini-selected, PDG only, PDG+complexity, PDG+inferability, full.
Mask granularity: single only, 85/15 single+pair, 95/5 single+triple, and the 80/15/5 mixture used in the main recipe.

Trajectory metrics: steps/edits per solved and unsolved task, recovery rate from negative observations (regex-matched stack traces, shell errors, harness failure strings), empty-patch rate, localization correctness.
Stratification of the 500 Verified tasks by gold-patch shape: 341 single-function, 88 multi-function single-file, 71 multi-file; Lite replication in appendix.

key_findings.finding: Function-aware FIM mid-training yields consistent SWE-Bench gains across model sizes, post-training pipelines, and base families.
key_findings.evidence: SWE-Bench-Verified/Lite improve by +2.80/+3.67 (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B + R2E-Gym), +3.00/+4.00 (14B + R2E-Gym), +5.30/+0.50 (7B + SWE-Smith), and +3.20/+5.40 (Qwen3-8B + SWE-Lego, reaching 35.0/32.7), each over the reproduced post-training-only baseline, averaged over three seeds.

key_findings.finding: Agentic post-training silently erodes non-agent and tool-use capabilities, and mid-training largely undoes this erosion, including on non-coding tool use despite a Python-only corpus.
key_findings.evidence: At 14B, R2E-Gym alone drops LiveCodeBench by 13.1, BFCL by 7.4, FullStackBench-EN by 6.08 vs. the Instruct ceiling (six-benchmark average -4.81); adding mid-training restores +11.10 LiveCodeBench, +1.94 OJBench, +3.90 tau-bench, +2.40 BFCL, +1.25 Terminal-Bench 2.0 (average 16.04 -> 19.56).

key_findings.finding: Gains concentrate on tasks requiring cross-function reasoning within a file, supporting the function-call/agent-loop isomorphism claim.
key_findings.evidence: On the 88 Verified tasks whose gold patch modifies >=2 functions in one file, pass rate rises 13.6% -> 22.7% (+9.1 pp), over 4x the +2.1 pp gain on 341 single-function tasks; the 71 multi-file tasks show no differential gain (~11.3% both), matching the within-file granularity of the masking.

key_findings.finding: The selection algorithm, not CoT distillation from a frontier teacher, is the dominant source of improvement.
key_findings.evidence: Ablation (A): FIM without any CoT already gains +1.18 average (about half the +2.43 Gemini-CoT gain) and self-generated CoT recovers 1.68 of 2.43 points; ablation (B): random masking averages 13.95 vs. 15.60 for full PDG+H+I, with PDG-only 14.85, +H 15.05, +I 15.35, and Gemini-selected 15.05.
